text:
alex_support: Heads up — customer acme-reports hit a build/CI failure after bumping the Go SDK to a v2 tag. They did a tagged release v2.0.1 and now `go build` fails in CI.

alex_support: Repro steps they sent: 
```
git clone git@github.com:acme/reports.git
cd reports
# module uses our SDK
go get github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go@v2.0.1
go build ./...
```

alex_support: Error snippet: 
```
go: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go@v2.0.1: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/@v/v2.0.1.info: 401 Unauthorized
# or locally: package github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go: module contains a go.mod file, but module path "github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go" does not match the path in that file: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/v2
```

maria_eng: @alex_support thanks — two likely things mixed up: 1) import path vs module path for v2 tags, 2) private/transitive replace causing proxy auth 401. Can you paste the SDK's go.mod from that tag and the project's go.mod?

alex_support: Pasted the SDK's go.mod from the v2.0.1 tag: 
```
module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/some/transitive v1.2.3
)
```

alex_support: And the customer's project go.mod references `github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go v2.0.1` (no /v2 suffix in import). They also have a `replace` in sdk-go (on that tag) pointing at a private fork: `replace github.com/some/transitive => github.com/acme/private-transitive v0.0.0-20250101010101-abcdef`

tim_devex: Yep — that combination explains both errors. For Go modules, when you publish a v2+ module the module path inside go.mod must include `/v2` (see https://go.dev/ref/mod#semantic-import-versioning). If the tag is v2.0.1 but module path is still `github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go` you'll get import/path mismatch.

tim_devex: The 401 is from proxy.golang.org trying to fetch the private transitive module from the replace target. Because the SDK's tagged go.mod references a replace to a private repo, proxy attempts to fetch and is unauthorized. Two options: remove the replace in the released tag (recommended) or instruct customers to set GOPRIVATE and proper credentialing so the proxy doesn't attempt the private fetch.

acme_dev_jane: @maria_eng fwiw we ran `go env GOPRIVATE` and it was empty. After setting `GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme/*` CI still failed because the SDK tag itself had the mismatch module path.

maria_eng: Short-term mitigation for the customer: pin to the pre-v2 pseudo-version (v1.x) that matches the module path, or use a temporary replace in their project to point to a local/forked copy of the SDK that fixes go.mod. Example workaround in their repo `go.mod`: 
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go => github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go v1.9.7-0.20250101-abcdef123456
```

maria_eng: Long-term fix: we should cut a new v2 release where the SDK's go.mod module line is `module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/v2` and remove any private replace directives from the published tag. Also prefer not to include replace directives in release tags — transforms build reproducibility and proxies.

alex_support: Customer asked if we can publish a patch; they need it ASAP for their deploy. Can engineering publish v2.0.2 with the corrected module path and no replace?

maria_eng: Yes, I can prepare a quick patch. Steps I'll take: 
1) update SDK go.mod to `module github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/v2`
2) remove the replace that points at acme private fork (move that into a non-tagged branch if needed)
3) run `gofmt`, `go test ./...` then tag `v2.0.2` and push.

maria_eng: Also will add a release note reminding maintainers not to include replace in tags and to update semver import path on major bumps.

release-bot: published release github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go v2.0.2 (tag: v2.0.2) :tada:

acme_dev_jane: Confirmed — after we updated our CI cache and ran `go get github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/v2@v2.0.2` the build succeeded. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:

tim_devex: Great. I'll file a short internal docs blurb for release process: check module path on major version, strip replace directives before tagging, and run `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go list -m -json all` to validate tags resolve from the public proxy (or document GOPRIVATE handling).

alex_support: Closing on our side — customer unblocked. Leaving notes for support playbook. :thumbsup:
